messages.author: 8bab6f3d22432f4e
messages.subject: Using Shiny and Shinydashboard
parts:
Hi,

I recently discovered shinydashboard http://rstudio.github.io/shinydashboard/index.html and I wanted to see if I could modify my current shiny app to use it.

However I'm not sure how to get the server side to work, for Shiny, the function shinyServer wraps the code defining the server in the file server.R, and
shinyUI wraps the code defining the UI in ui.R and runApp() in Rstudio works.

Inspecting several source codes of example shinydashboard apps here: https://github.com/jcheng5/crandash

They don't use shinyServer(), and have files like global.R and the server code in server.R is simply contained in

function(input, output, session){} - no shinyServer() use.

What is the right way to use shinydashboard in an already existing app? The website only shows you how to use it for a single file app:

# app.R ##
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(),
  dashboardSidebar(),
  dashboardBody()
)

server <- function(input, output) { }

shinyApp(ui, server)

but doesn’t tell me what I need to do if I have separate files ui.R and server.R and so on to get it to work with runApp().

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Using Shiny and Shinydashboard
parts:
Sorry for not explaining this. These two server.R files are identical:

# server.R 1
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
   ...
})

# server.R 2
function(input, output, session) {
   ...
}

As long as the server function is the last expression in server.R, the shinyServer call is now optional. The same is true for shinyUI in ui.R; it's optional as long as the last expression is your UI.
